title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Consider the market for energy drinks shown. Which letter represents consumer surplus at the market equilibrium?
explanation: Consumer surplus is the area between the demand curve and the price, up to the equilibrium quantity — region A.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letter represents producer surplus at the market equilibrium?
explanation: Producer surplus is the area between the price and the supply curve, up to the equilibrium quantity — region B.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Energy drinks are addictive, so the government places a per-unit tax on them (shown by the S + tax curve). Using the diagram, what is the size of the tax per can?
explanation: The per-unit tax is the vertical gap between the original supply curve and the S+tax curve — $2.00 per can.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: After the tax, what price do consumers pay per can?
explanation: After the tax the price consumers pay rises to where demand meets the S+tax curve — $6.00 per can.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: By how much does the tax reduce the quantity of energy drinks traded?
explanation: The tax lifts the price and cuts trade: quantity falls to where demand meets S+tax — a drop of 10 million cans.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letters represent the loss of consumer surplus caused by the tax?
explanation: Consumers lose the area between the old and new price up to the new quantity, plus the surplus on trades no longer made — regions B + D.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letters represent the loss of producer surplus caused by the tax?
explanation: Producers lose the area between the old and new price they keep, plus the surplus on trades no longer made — regions C + E.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letters represent the government's tax revenue?
explanation: Tax revenue is the per-unit tax times the quantity still traded — the rectangle B + C.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letters represent the deadweight loss caused by the tax?
explanation: The tax cuts trade below the efficient quantity; the lost gains from trade are the deadweight loss, regions D + E.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Instead, suppose the government imposes a quota limiting energy drink sales to 30 million cans. Which letter(s) show the new consumer surplus?
explanation: Limiting sales raises the price consumers pay, so consumer surplus shrinks to the triangle above that price — region A.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Under the 30 million can quota, which letter(s) show the new producer surplus?
explanation: Under the quota producers sell fewer cans but at a higher price, giving producer surplus of B + C.

title: Market for energy drinks
questionText: Which letters represent the deadweight loss created by the quota?
explanation: The quota holds trade below the efficient quantity, so the lost gains from trade — the deadweight loss — are regions D + E.
